The pilot was authorized under the NSF Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (NSF SBIR/STTR) Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program. NSF pioneered the federal SBIR/STTR model in the late 1970s, demonstrating an approach that Congress formally established government-wide in 1982 for federal agencies with significant extramural research and development budgets. Today, NSF SBIR/STTR provides early-stage funding to technology startups and small businesses to de-risk promising technologies, develop prototypes, and translate research and development into products and services with commercial and societal impact. In recent years, $1.6 billion in NSF SBIR/STTR investments over a five-year period helped support startups in attracting more than $36 billion in subsequent funding — demonstrating the program's ability to leverage federal R&D investments and accelerate technologies toward the marketplace.
